results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 46 outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs, in spec order (introduction p01-p06, sections reasons through wrong, conclusion p43-p48); structure.json's deterministic check also passes.

The only unit marked two_ideas is What to Take Away ¶4 (p46). It is a two-bullet list headed 'The author's synthesis', and the spec's controlling idea for p46 itself holds both items (plan backwards from the first peak; the reconciliation job as the main deliverable) under one idea, the author's own judgement. As a list unit it has one controlling idea. No other unit was marked.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: reasons to S1; scene to S3/S5; failures to S2; strangler and pieces to S3; data to S4; integrations to S4/S5; cutover to S5; practice to S3-S5; stages to S6; wrong to S3-S5; the introduction and conclusion state and synthesize the thesis. No orphan paragraph.

results.draft_locus: In Practice: The OMS and PIM Introductions at Kestrel & Pine ¶5
results.quote: the marketplace, D2C and wholesale rows are three diverted seams, the freeze holds them through Black Friday, and the last column shows that every step had a way back
results.finding: The sentence that explains the OMS table says what the table shows, but both flow readers report that the table does not bear it out: it has seven rows that do not map onto the five phases ('Divert all' has no row, 'Change freeze' is not a phase), and its last column reads 'Nothing to reverse' and 'Not needed' for some rows, contradicting 'every step had a way back'. The explanation is placed before a table the reader has not seen and misdescribes it.

All other evidence is explained: the reasons table is framed by the test it applies; each case quotation (Target, Finish Line, M&S, Hobbycraft) is followed by what it shows, and the case table is interpreted by the Burned Bridge paragraph; Fowler's and Thoughtworks' quotations are followed by why feature parity produces the Burned Bridge; Zalando ('the strangler in production at a large retailer'); the App That Wrote Stock ('the systems diverge and nobody is told'); the phase, data and stage tables are introduced by the claim they support; the 1,900 variants, the 1.4% differences and the history import each carry their meaning. Minor: the Figure 3 caption ('Five of the seven migrations') momentarily clashes with the seven-row table (flow-A 18).

Every declared transition_in is expressed at the start of its unit and picks up the declared known information: e.g. 'A plan therefore starts' (problem_solution), 'Kestrel & Pine answered that question in February' (example), 'The second warning is' (additional_support), 'Noor's rules guard against a danger the public record documents' (elaboration), 'What the cases share' (conclusion_summary), 'They sound like a parallel run and are the opposite in risk' (contrast), 'With the phases set' / 'The table's last row needs a section of its own' / 'With the data loaded and the integrations listed' (elaboration, elaboration, sequence), 'The rollback has a limit' (contrast), 'Kestrel & Pine's migrations went to plan. When one does not' (contrast), 'The opening asked' (conclusion_summary). Weakest but acceptable: M&S's contrast ('The shape here is different: nothing crashed') comes after the case label and two sentences, not at the very start; the pieces section opens on 'two systems hold the same fact' without naming seams.

Hand-off to commerce-scaling-stages: 'Migrations are the moments when a merchant moves from one scale stage to the next and feels it. The next chapter steps back to the stages themselves...' carries over this chapter's migrations and introduces the stages, the decisions that change, the signals and Kestrel & Pine's path, as hand_off declares (elaboration).

results.finding: 'Strangler approach' is on does_not_know and is used in the KEY POINTS callout, with 'router' and 'copy of the flow', before the strangler section defines it. The body defines all three later. Quote from terms.md; the callout is not in structure.json's draft_text.

results.quote: The new hub's SaaS has an incident during the window.
results.finding: 'SaaS' is not among the audience's known glosses and is never expanded.

results.quote: The search index, a cache or the data warehouse still reads the old owner
results.finding: 'Cache' and 'data warehouse' (and 'search index') are not in already_knows and are not glossed here; the cross-links point forward to later chapters.

The other terms on does_not_know are explained at or before first use: seam, shadow ('where nobody acts on it'), change freeze, the Burned Bridge, strangler fig, the Thoughtworks moves, feature parity, parallel run, dual writes, cutover, go/no-go, rollback, 404/410 and SEO; the public cases are introduced with dates and sources. Remaining terms.md items (Fowler/Thoughtworks, Zalando's identity, 'non-compliant', 'Go-based', one-way hashes, Retail Dive/Week, Missoni, the unnamed Price Drift) are names or incidental words whose meaning the sentence carries; not genuine failures. Over-explanation of PIM/OMS, idempotent and Amazon noted as minor style points.

The introduction opens on a puzzling scenario (two systems that can both send an order to the warehouse), bridges to a transfer of responsibility, introduces the case, states the thesis and gives a roadmap with evidence; none of the weak patterns.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', introduces no new subtopic, does not end on a restated thesis alone, and its lists (established / depends on context / author's synthesis / questions) are labelled synthesis, not a grab bag; the order sent twice is recalled from the body, not new evidence.

p43 states what no single section states (every step answers one question: which system may act on a fact now; one sender per seam), and p46 says why it matters (plan backwards from the first peak; the reconciliation stays in production and makes the next migration cheaper). Note: the spec's so_what clause that the same plan applies to introducing a hub, not only to replatforming, is not said explicitly.

'The opening asked how to change who sends work to the warehouse without two parcels or a missed order' returns to the hook and answers it with one sender per seam and the order the old path had sent twice, as callback declares.

The intro reader predicts the sections in roadmap order (reasons, Noor's plan for PIM in Q3 and OMS in Q4 after the March 2027 decision to keep the platform, three failures and an avoided case, strangler-phases-seven data migrations-integrations-cutover/rollback, the 2027 timeline, scale, what goes wrong), the evidence (dated press reports, Fowler and Thoughtworks patterns, Zalando's posts, Kestrel & Pine's ~800 orders a day) and a practical, sober tone, and frames migration as a transfer of responsibility for a fact. Only nuance not reproduced: that the documented failures were not feature failures.

The reader names the Burned Bridge (one date, first real load at peak, no way back), re-created history firing side effects (import read-only with original numbers), dual writes diverging silently (prefer one writer and a copied flow; idempotent and reconciled if unavoidable), and replaces the plan with shadow, a parallel run reconciling by cause, smallest channel first, written go/no-go, a timed rehearsed rollback, continuous order numbers, a freeze through Black Friday and the old path kept operable through the peak. Only the App That Wrote Stock is not named; the mechanism is.

The reader sorts all six: stock as ownership/system of record, unfindable orders as an OMS-beside problem, slow Black Friday a maybe (usually integrations), vendor end-of-life a reason on the vendor's date (Magento 1, 30 June 2020), forked core a reason but rebuild vs leave, agency not a reason (check who is paid and who owns the joins). Matches expected.

The reader gives each kind of data with its identifier, owner or trap (SKU/GTIN, silent price drift, password hashes, consent with proof, orders as read-only history, gift cards to the cent, URL redirects, integrations re-pointed or mimicked) and explains the rollback limit: records accumulate in the new system, copies narrow but do not close the gap, the cheap-rollback window closes on its own. Matches expected.
